ABSTRACT
A simple and mild catalytic S
N
2 ′ -type displacement of propargyl halides with organotitanium reagents is re -
ported. The S
N
2 ′ -type displacement of propargyl bromides with organotitanium reagents mediated by CuI (2 mol 
%)/MePPh
2
(4 mol%) in dichloro methane afforded multi-substituted allenes in good yields (up to 95 %) at 40 
◦
C 
for 5 h. The aryls bearing electron-donating or electron-withdrawing groups in aryltitanium reagents gave multi- 
substituted allenes in good yields. In addition, the di-substituted allenes bearing a naphthyl group was obtained 
in 54 – 99 % selectivities with isolated yields of 43 – 83 %. The process was simple and easily performed, and it 
provides an efficient method for the synthesis of di-substituted allene derivatives. On the basis of the experi -
mental results, a possible catalytic cycle has been proposed.
1. Introduction
Allenes are a kind of very useful organic compounds. As important 
synthetic fragments and functional groups, allenes have been widely 
applied for many transformations in organic synthesis [ 1 , 2 ]. Allene 
moieties have also been found in many of natural products, pharma -
ceuticals [ 3 ], and optical materials [ 4 ]. Due to the wide range of ap -
plications of allenes, the synthesis of allenes has attracted great attention 
of many organic chemists and medical chemists. Developing efficient 
reactions for the synthesis of allenes from simple and readily available 
organic compounds is very important. Based on various utilities of 
allenes, many effective synthetic methodologies of synthesis allene 
compounds have been reported [ 5 , 6 ]. Typical synthetic protocols for 
substituted allenes include elimination of allylic compounds [ 7 ], isom -
erization of alkynes [ 8 ], a reaction of aldehydes and terminal alkynes 
[ 9 ], and S
N
2 ′ -type displacement of propargylic compounds [ 10 ]. Among 
these methods hitherto developed, the metal-catalyzed S
N
2 ′ -type 
displacement of propargyl alcohol derivatives with organometal species 
is one of the most generally useful one ( Scheme 1 ). However, there are 
two competing possible reaction pathways. The successful application of 
such a substitution reaction relies on the choice of catalyst and/or 
organometallic reagents to selectively produce either allene product 2 or 
alkyne product 3 . Therefore, the development of rapid and more effi -
cient procedures for the synthesis of allenes still remains a challenge.
Our previous studies show that organotitanium reagents are highly 
efficient nucleophiles for cross-coupling reactions with organic halides 
[ 11 ], and the investigations have demonstrated that copper is a good 
catalytic metal [ 12 ]. To continue our effort to develop coupling re -
actions using reactive organometallic reagents (6r,6s [ 12-13 ]), we 
herein report a CuI (2 mol%)/MePPh
2 
(4 mol%) catalyzed S
N
2 ′ -type 
displacement of propargyl halides with organotitanium reagents at 40 
◦
C in short reaction time with good yields for the synthesis of allenes. 
The process was simple and easily performed, and it provides an efficient 
method for the synthesis of substituted allene derivatives.

3. Conclusions
In conclusion, a copper-catalyzed the S
N
2 ′ substitute reaction of 
propargyl bromides with aryltitanium reagents was reported. The S
N
2 ′ 
substitute reactions of aromatic propargyl bromides and aliphatic 
propargyl bromides with aryltitanium afforded di-substituted allenes in 
good yields (39–95 %) with high selectivities (up to 99:1). The S
N
2 ′ 
substitute reactions of aromatic propargyl bromides 1 (d,e,f) producing 
the di-substituted allenes of 3 (da-fh) in 39–83 % isolated yields with 
selectivities of up to 99 %. The S
N
2’ substitute reactions of aliphatic 
propargyl bromides 1 (a,b,c) with aryltitaniums can proceeded 
smoothly to give the di-substituted allenes of 3 (aa-cg) in excellent 
yields (up to 95 %) with high selectivities (up to 99 %). More impor -
tantly, the reaction was found to be effective in gram-scale synthesis. 
Notably, no other co-catalysts and additives are necessary in the present 
procedure. This methodology provides useful procedure for the syn -
thesis of di-substituted allenes. Further studies on the application of this 
catalyst to other organotitanium reagents are currently under way.
